content: 1. For infections caused by Staphylococcus haemolyticus, the following treatment regimens are recommended: Administer 1.5–2 g of intravenous (IV) antibiotics every 6–8 hours. Alternative regimen (1): Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) at a dose of 4–5 mg/kg IV every 6–12 hours. Alternative regimen (2): Doxycycline at a dose of 100–200 mg IV every 12–24 hours. 2. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus strains that are susceptible to glycopeptides: The preferred regimen is vancomycin at a dose of 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 hours. 3. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus haemolyticus strains that are resistant to glycopeptides: Preferred regimen (1): Daptomycin at a dose of 4–6 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. Preferred regimen (2): Linezolid at a dose of 600 mg orally (PO) or IV every 12 hours. 4. For urinary tract infections caused by Staphylococcus saprophyticus: Preferred regimen (1): Cephalexin 500 mg PO four times daily (qid). Preferred regimen (2): Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO twice daily (bid). Preferred regimen (3): TMP-SMX 160–800 mg PO bid. Alternative regimen: Levofloxacin 500 mg PO once daily (qd). 5. For dental abscesses caused by Streptococcus anginosus: The preferred regimen is penicillin V 500 mg PO qid. Alternative regimen: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 hours. 6. For brain abscesses caused by Streptococcus anginosus: Preferred regimen (1): Penicillin G at a dose of 18–24 million units per day IV, divided every 4–6 hours. Preferred regimen (2): Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 hours. 7. For food poisoning caused by Bacillus cereus: Food poisoning is typically self-limiting and does not require antibiotic therapy. 8. For bacteremia caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen is vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. Note (1): Bacillus cereus is commonly resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics. Note (2): Pseudobacteremia is often transient and usually results from contaminated blood cultures, gloves, or syringes. 9. For meningitis or brain abscess caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen is vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. Note: Blood culture isolates are often contaminants unless proven otherwise, especially in intravenous drug users. 10. For endophthalmitis caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen includes intravitreal clindamycin (450 μg) and gentamicin (400 μg), or intravitreal dexamethasone, combined with vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. Note: Ophthalmological consultation, ocular fluid cultures, early vitrectomy, and intravitreal antibiotics are essential. 11. For endocarditis caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen is vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Note: Most blood cultures in intravenous drug users are contaminants or represent transient bacteremia. 12. For soft tissue infections caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen is vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. 13. For pneumonia caused by Bacillus cereus: The preferred regimen is vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV every 12 hours. Alternative regimen: Clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. 14. For infections caused by Elizabethkingia meningoseptica: Specific regimens were not provided in the text.
